description: The unit tests in test/inngest.test.js could NOT and did NOT catch the runtime-crashing adapter bug (originally `inngest/express` serve mounted on a raw http.createServer, which throws 'res.status is not a function' at request time). Test F (lines 221-243) only does a SOURCE STRING check `src.includes('/api/inngest')` — it passes with EITHER adapter and never imports server.js nor calls inngestHandler(req,res). No test executes the mounted handler against a fake req/res, so the integration crash was invisible to `npm test`. The express-vs-node defect was only caught by the live dev-server E2E, not the test suite. This is a structural test-coverage gap: a unit test that exercised `inngestServe({client,functions})` then invoked the returned handler with a mock {req,res} would have caught it.

evidence.snippet: test("server.js source contains the /api/inngest mount", () => { const src = fs.readFileSync(...); assert.ok(src.includes("/api/inngest")); });
